thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — I opened a docs PR with embedding-shard guidance + a short migration checklist for shardable models (Nebula3b, Nova-embeds, etc.). Need eyes on limits, compatibility notes, and the SDK snippets. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/789 :memo:

alvin: Thanks — will take a look. Can you paste the key bench numbers here? Also should the SDK default to `shard_count=1` or `auto`?

maya: Bench summary (copied from bench artifact): avg latency per embed (8k tokens batch): 12ms/shard on A100, throughput: 85k embeds/s across 8 shards, memory per shard ~6.2GB. I left the SDK default as explicit 1 in the snippet to avoid surprising behavior.

samir: Quick compatibility note: Dedicated customers that pin model variants might see coldstart KV penalties if they increase shard_count without warmup. Suggest adding a line under "Compatibility" about pre-warming / cache-populate. :warning:

sophia: I went through the SDK snippet, rewrote the python + ts examples to include `shard_count` param and a short fallback example. Snippet below — please sanity-check formatting: 

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
emb = client.embeddings.create(model='nebula3b', input=["a","b"], shard_count=4)
# emb.data -> list of vectors (length == len(input) * shard_count)
```

```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk'
const rw = new Redwood(process.env.RW_KEY)
const resp = await rw.embeddings.create({ model: 'nebula3b', input: ['a','b'], shard_count: 4 })
// flatten/sum/aggregate per-shard vectors as needed
```

doc-bot: lint-check: passed. Link-checker: found 1 broken link — `/model-catalog/nebula3b` -> update to `/models/nebula3b`. Flagged and auto-fixed in PR diff.

kai: Bench numbers look reasonable. Can you add a quick cost estimate example (USD per 1M queries) so customers can compare shard vs single-shard cost? I can add one if you want.

maya: Good call — I added a small table in the PR and a worked example: 1M queries, avg tokens 64 -> estimate $X with 4 shards vs $Y with 1 shard (I used our pricing model assumptions). Also added a minimal migration checklist: 
- export existing embeddings (example CLI)
- pick shard_count based on throughput/cost
- re-encode/backfill vectors (suggest background job & backpressure)
- update retrieval code to aggregate/shard-aware queries
- monitor recall/regression with evaluation prompts

Is that too prescriptive?

samir: Not too prescriptive. Add a short note: "If you must maintain backward compatibility, serve both single-shard and sharded indexes for a transitional period." Also add fallback behavior when query-time shard_count mismatches: runtime should fall back to scalar retrieval (documented) instead of failing. :thumbsup:

sophia: On naming: standardized param as `shard_count` across docs and snippets (not `shards`). I also adjusted the TS example to show async streaming and a small aggregation helper snippet for consumers.

maya: Thanks — updated per comments and fixed the broken link. Will merge after 1 more approval. @alvin @kai can you PTAL? Targeting 2026-04-01 release for the model-catalog refresh.

alvin: LGTM from docs perspective. Tiny grammar nit in migration checklist, I'll approve after CI passes.

doc-bot: merge queued: will attempt auto-merge in 2 hours once approvals >=2 and CI green.

maya: Awesome — appreciate the quick reviews. I added a short note in the PR description about Dedicated coldstart impacts and a pointer to the pre-warm script (internal link).
